The title reproduces the parent's atlas title 'Algebraic cycles, pure and mixed motives' exactly, the area motives is a galaxy id, and the brief is 371 words. What makes this route right is that it does not open a roadmap: it coalesces with MotivesRigidAnalyticPartII as proposed by PAPER-BINDA-KATO-VEZZANI-25 — same id, same title, same parent and area — and says so in its first sentence, adding Berkovich motives as a branch that reuses the Part II's formal layers and reproves several of its planned endpoints (motivic Fontaine–Wintenberger in Propositions 6.8 and 9.7, generation by good reduction in Proposition 10.1, motivic nearby cycles in Theorem 1.14). notes: Accept, no corrections needed. The recorded hash of arXiv 2412.03382v3 reproduces (440b4a82…) and I re-extracted all 65 pages. Structure: 55 items (50 missing, 5 planned), every missing item routed exactly once, all seven stage ids exist, all five planned layer ids exist, the Part II parent exists and the proposed title reproduces its atlas title exactly, the area is a galaxy id, and check_paper.py passes. Two planned items (4 and 6) appear in the TB.0/TB.1 source route; that is not a defect but the provision in PROTOCOL §16 that a source route may also name planned items the paper is a good source for. Coverage: 167 numbered environments appear in the text and all but one are carried into items — Examples 3.5 and 3.7 sit inside item 9 ('Examples 3.4–3.8, Proposition 3.9'), Corollaries 8.1–8.2 inside item 30, and the single exception is Remark 1.4, a comparison with the derived category of v-sheaves in the introduction, which states no mathematics the roadmap has to plan. Locators: 143 name-and-page checks land on exactly the page given; the misses are my own parsing of 'Theorem 2.14, Corollary 2.15' lists, plus E2's proof of Theorem 6.3, stated on p.35 and proved on p.36. I sampled the statements against the paper and they are faithful, including the conventions in item 1 — Definition 2.1 does ask only for |0| = 0, |−1| ≤ 1, submultiplicativity and subadditivity, with norm-nonincreasing maps. All three findings are confirmed at their locators: the unescaped \pm printed as 'pm1' on p.14, where the same ring is written with ± one clause later; P¹_A for P¹_C in three places on pp.36–37, where the ambient is A¹_C over an algebraically closed field and no Banach ring A is in scope; and Example 3.6's claim that ∏^Ban K(x) is totally disconnected for any Banach ring A, which fails for a discrete A because Definition 3.10(i) requires analytic, and which the paper's own Example 3.4 repairs by arc-covering any nonzero Banach ring by A[T^{±1}]_{1/2}. Nothing was corrected, rejected or deleted, and I add no finding: I read §§2–3, 6 and 8 around the findings and the statements the routes cite, not all 65 pages line by line. The JAMS version is paywalled and was not compared, as the extraction records.
